examples.scenario: Parcel intersects two 5km tiles but only one is downloaded.
examples.reason: Coverage union must fully cover the parcel before raster sampling.

examples.scenario: Tile name is guessed from a coordinate string without checking extent metadata.
examples.reason: Use BNG grid derivation plus authoritative extent/os_ref metadata.

examples.scenario: FeatureServer query returns more than the service record limit and only first page is kept.
examples.reason: Pagination/record-count handling is mandatory.

examples.scenario: DSM extent layer is queried instead of DTM extent layer.
examples.reason: Bare-earth terrain acquisition must bind the DTM layer.

examples.scenario: FeatureServer filename is stored but os_ref is discarded.
examples.reason: Keep filename and authoritative grid reference together.

examples.scenario: Flown start/end dates are dropped after selecting a time-stamped survey.
examples.reason: Capture dates are temporal provenance.

examples.scenario: pt_spacing is treated as exact raster cell size without checking the raster.
examples.reason: Point spacing/density and raster grid resolution are different concepts.

examples.scenario: transform field is missing but elevation is labelled ODN/OSGM15.
examples.reason: Survey-specific transformation must be explicit.

examples.scenario: geoid field is missing for a historical survey.
examples.reason: Historical survey vertical conversion cannot be inferred.

examples.scenario: filepath returned by extent metadata changes but cached raster is reused.
examples.reason: Re-resolve and digest the selected source artifact.

examples.scenario: The FeatureServer polygon intersects parcel only at a sliver but coverage completeness is assumed.
examples.reason: Compute actual parcel coverage by selected extents/tiles.

examples.scenario: A WMS preview colour is converted to an elevation value.
examples.reason: EA states preview is an image and cannot be queried.

examples.scenario: WCS output is accepted without identifying the underlying survey/tile source.
examples.reason: Service numeric output needs terminal source lineage.

examples.scenario: OGC API feature is used as if it were the elevation raster bytes.
examples.reason: Discovery metadata and elevation payload are separate evidence.

examples.scenario: Browser Download All only returns first tile because pop-ups are blocked.
examples.reason: Verify enumerated tile count and downloaded archive count.

examples.scenario: Downloaded zip exists but HTTP/status/content length were not recorded.
examples.reason: Capture transport and immutable digest evidence.

examples.scenario: Zip digest is recorded but GeoTIFF member digest is not.
examples.reason: Terminal raster member identity must also be pinned.

examples.scenario: GeoTIFF is digested but metadata GeoPackage is ignored.
examples.reason: Pair raster with spatial/temporal metadata index.

examples.scenario: Metadata GeoPackage is parsed but its schema/extent is not validated.
examples.reason: Validate schema and spatial/temporal relation to tile.

examples.scenario: Raster CRS readback differs from advertised EPSG:27700.
examples.reason: Downloaded bytes override assumptions from catalogue labels.

examples.scenario: Raster has no proven vertical unit but catalogue says metres.
examples.reason: Reconcile file metadata with authoritative product metadata.

examples.scenario: Two time-stamped surveys overlap and latest flag alone chooses one.
examples.reason: Use semantics, coverage, QC, resolution, transform and recency.

examples.scenario: Newest survey has DSM only and is selected for terrain.
examples.reason: DTM bare-earth semantics precede recency.

examples.scenario: Older 25cm DTM and newer 2m DTM overlap; 25cm is always chosen by resolution.
examples.reason: Resolution alone does not establish fitness/accuracy.

examples.scenario: Point cloud exists but historic raster has no confirmed matching cloud.
examples.reason: Treat cloud matching as optional verified evidence.

examples.scenario: 1 ppsqm point density is described as 1m DTM resolution.
examples.reason: EA explicitly distinguishes irregular point density from grid resolution.

examples.scenario: OS Terrain 5 benchmark tile is compared without release/flying-date metadata.
examples.reason: Independent QA must be reproducible.

examples.scenario: OS Terrain 5 aux.xml min/max are used as actual tile extrema.
examples.reason: OS documents those statistics as styling aids.

examples.scenario: OS Terrain 50 is upsampled and used to fill missing EA parcel cells.
examples.reason: Coarse benchmark cannot fabricate terminal EA coverage.

examples.scenario: A dataset licence is assumed from another EA dataset.
examples.reason: Capture selected dataset licence/attribution record.

examples.scenario: Source URL is kept but download timestamp is omitted.
examples.reason: Acquisition time is part of reproducible web evidence.

examples.scenario: Same URL later serves changed bytes and cache is trusted.
examples.reason: Digest/readback immutable local cache content.

examples.scenario: Multi-tile parcel uses tiles from different survey years but this is hidden.
examples.reason: Expose every contributing survey/date.

examples.scenario: Multi-tile parcel uses different geoid/transform generations without reconciliation.
examples.reason: Reconcile before cross-tile extrema comparison.

examples.scenario: Parcel coverage is 99.9% and the small uncovered area is ignored.
examples.reason: Terminal extrema require proven coverage of the defined parcel sampling domain.

examples.scenario: Only bounding-box intersection is used and polygon holes/outside cells enter sampling.
examples.reason: Tile discovery bbox is not final parcel cell membership.

examples.scenario: FeatureServer current view changes after initial query and no response digest exists.
examples.reason: Persist query parameters and response digest.

examples.scenario: Downloaded file is renamed and provenance path is lost.
examples.reason: Retain authoritative filename/path plus local immutable name.

examples.scenario: Source acquisition readiness 99.99 is reported as 99.99% measured elevation accuracy.
examples.reason: Readiness is preparation confidence, not target measurement accuracy.

examples.scenario: Height difference is published before canonical point, boundary, tile coverage, raster/index digests and runner outputs exist.
examples.reason: Real numeric/business output remains fail-closed.
